analysis: What changed versus the 9:00 AM brief: Thursday closed red after the midday flip to green faded — S&P 500 -0.35% to 7,592.40, Nasdaq -0.39%, Dow -0.36%, Russell -1.66%, with the VIX jumping to 18.70 (+1.21) and the 10-year closing above 5.10% for the first time in this stretch. The Nvidia story is now a two-part trade: the governance shock is priced (NVDA -4.34% Thursday on 740M shares, recovering from a $148.80 open low) and the stock is bouncing +1.87% premarket, but the 8-K gave no reason and no severance, keeping the succession question open into the Nov 17 earnings print. The bigger headwind is still rates, not Nvidia: the 10-year at 5.12% with FedWatch pricing a 100% December hike is what is pinning small caps and crypto (BTC -3.44% in 24h). The two after-hours earnings tests split: Cisco beat and raised on AI networking demand but faded to -1.72% premarket, while Applied Materials beat and guided above and held roughly flat — the market is no longer rewarding AI beats automatically. New overnight pressure: Microsoft's 365 outage is into day two with fixes 'not taking as expected' (MSFT -1.53% premarket), and a fresh Trump tariff threat against Mexico adds a macro wildcard. Signal vs noise: the 8-K, both earnings prints, the outage, and the PPI setup are confirmed signal. The Trump/Cook succession post and the Srouji report remain theater and single-source respectively. Friday's PPI is the next real test — a hot print with the 10-year above 5.1% would likely hit rate-sensitive names hardest.

headlines.headline: Nvidia is rebounding premarket, +1.87%, after closing Thursday at $166.19 (-4.34%) on 740M shares, well off the $148.80 open low. The Form 8-K confirms the board accepted Huang's resignation on Nov 11 with no reason given and no severance disclosed; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO, Harvey Jones is board chair, and the Nov 17 earnings date is unchanged.
headlines.why_it_matters: Buyers are defending above the panic low and the stock is bouncing, but the 8-K's silence on reason and severance keeps the governance overhang alive into Tuesday's earnings print.

headlines.headline: Microsoft's global 365 outage is into a second day: Outlook, Teams, Copilot and SharePoint remain degraded, and Microsoft said its fixes are 'not taking as expected' with capacity not yet back to baseline. No malicious activity is indicated; Downdetector logged ~130,000 Outlook reports at Thursday's peak. MSFT is -1.53% premarket to ~$515.02.
headlines.why_it_matters: A second day of failed fixes turns a one-day outage into a reliability story for the world's biggest productivity suite — a sentiment drag on the stock and a reminder that cloud concentration is a single point of failure.

headlines.headline: Cisco beat and raised after the close: fiscal Q1 adjusted EPS $1.40 vs $1.33 expected, revenue $18.52B (+24%) vs ~$18.1B expected; full-year revenue guidance lifted to $74.8-75.8B and hyperscaler AI infrastructure revenue guided to $9B in fiscal 2027, more than double last year. Shares popped after hours, then faded to -1.72% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: A clean AI-demand beat that the market handed back — the fade says investors are now skeptical of AI infrastructure prints, not cheering them, which matters for the whole buildout trade.

headlines.headline: Applied Materials beat and guided above: fiscal Q4 adjusted EPS $4.16 vs $4.06 expected, record revenue $10.41B (+53%) vs $10.30B expected; January-quarter revenue guided to ~$11.1B vs ~$10.89B expected, with EPS guided to $4.35 +/- $0.20 vs $4.25. Shares are +0.14% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: Chip-equipment demand is holding up — a steadier AI-spending read than Cisco's fade, and a counterweight to the Nebius capex scare from Thursday.

headlines.headline: President Trump said Mexico must stop migrant caravans heading north or face 'immediately doubled' tariffs, writing on Truth Social that 'there will be no leniency.'
headlines.why_it_matters: A fresh tariff threat overnight adds a macro wildcard into a tape already nervous about rates — it can move Mexico-exposed names and the broader risk tone if it escalates.

headlines.headline: October PPI lands at 8:30 AM ET today, expected +0.4% month-over-month. The 10-year is at 5.12% and the CME FedWatch tool prices a 100% likelihood of a Fed rate hike after the December meeting.
headlines.why_it_matters: With yields above 5.1% and a hike fully priced, a hot PPI print is the most direct threat to the open — it would validate the rate pressure that sank small caps Thursday.

headlines.headline: Cerebras (CBRS) is +17.7% premarket after reporting Q3 revenue of $210.8M, beating estimates, with cloud revenue up 272%, and raising full-year guidance. Nu Holdings (NU) is +3.51% premarket after a mixed Q3 print (EPS $0.22 on revenue $5.82B).
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI trade is splitting: a smaller AI-infra name with real cloud growth is being rewarded sharply while the megacap chip leader is still working through a governance discount.

headlines.headline: The other megacaps are mixed premarket: Alphabet +1.09% to ~$301.97 and Amazon +1.09% to ~$270.34, Apple +0.36% to ~$356.15. Thursday's closes: Alphabet $298.70 (+1.79%), Tesla $397.45 (+1.69%), Amazon $267.44 (+0.48%), Microsoft $523.00 (+0.36%), Apple $354.88 (-0.21%), Meta $623.61 (-0.82%).
headlines.why_it_matters: Five of six megacaps closed green Thursday despite the Nvidia shock — the rotation-within-big-tech read is intact, with only the outage-hit Microsoft dragging premarket.
